short_summary: A recent university study reveals that grocery prices in Israel surged significantly over a four-year period, far outpacing previous trends and placing a heavy burden on consumers.

sources.name: Walla
sources.title: סיכום קדנציה מזעזע: מחירי המזון בישראל זינקו ב-19% בארבע שנים

paragraphs: Recent academic research reveals that grocery prices in Israel surged dramatically over a four-year period, marking a striking acceleration compared to previous years. According to a study conducted by researchers at Tel Aviv University, a representative basket of eighty popular consumer goods increased in price by nearly twenty percent across neighborhood shops and online platforms, while discount chains saw an increase of roughly fourteen percent. By contrast, price growth during the preceding four years was remarkably modest, hovering around three to four percent depending on the retail channel.

Researchers tracked prices across approximately seven hundred supermarket branches using comprehensive market data that included promotions and discounts. The findings highlight extraordinary price jumps for everyday items. For instance, a standard milk chocolate bar manufactured by Elite experienced an increase of nearly seventy-eight percent in neighborhood stores. Other household staples, including infant formula, coffee, spreads, and frozen pastries, also recorded substantial upward price movements, translating to hundreds of additional shekels per shopping basket for identical items.

The study also examined the significant price gaps existing among various retail chains. While discount supermarkets generally offered more affordable totals than neighborhood shops or online delivery services, the rate of increase affected all purchase channels uniformly. Furthermore, researchers compared the retail price trends with official statistics regarding food manufacturing costs. While production costs rose at a much slower pace over the same timeframe, retail prices climbed sharply, prompting questions regarding the explanations provided by food manufacturers and retail chains.

According to the study's authors, multiple factors contributed to the inflationary wave, including increases in municipal taxes, electricity, water, fuel, and value-added tax rates. However, researchers emphasize that these official inputs fail to fully explain the extent of the price hikes. They point out that during this period, the Israeli shekel strengthened and global food commodity prices retreated from their previous peaks, conditions that should have theoretically moderated import costs and reined in domestic prices.

Beyond economic factors, the researchers argue that inadequate governmental intervention and a decline in public and media attention played a critical role. With the administration largely preoccupied with political crises and wartime challenges, the issue of the high cost of living slipped down the national agenda, allowing food companies to raise prices with minimal public pushback. Data published by the State Comptroller previously indicated that grocery baskets in Israel were already well above the OECD average before this recent wave began.

Although the rate of price increases showed signs of slowing down toward the latter part of the period, the accumulated hikes have caused severe financial strain, particularly for lower-income families. Because households in the lowest income quintile allocate a substantially larger share of their monthly budget to food purchases compared to wealthier households, the ongoing expenses remain disproportionately burdensome. The researchers conclude that tackling the cost of living requires genuine governmental action, enhanced market competition, and the removal of structural barriers within the food industry.

facts.fact: A study by Tel Aviv University researchers Itai Ater and Adi Omer found that a basket of 80 popular grocery products in Israel increased in price by 19% to 19.6% between September 2022 and August 2026, roughly five times the rate of the preceding four years.
During the previous four-year period, prices had risen by only about 2.8% to 4.3% depending on the channel.
Neighborhood stores and online shopping saw the steepest price hikes at nearly 19-20%, while discount chains rose by 14.5%.
Specific items such as Elite milk chocolate bars surged by up to 78% in neighborhood shops over the period.
Researchers noted that the surge far outpaced production cost increases and coincided with a government distracted by political crises and war, alongside a lack of public pressure.
Data from the State Comptroller showed Israeli grocery baskets were already roughly 37% higher than the OECD average in 2024.
Lower-income households spend a significantly larger portion of their monthly budget on food, making the steep increases particularly burdensome.
